findings.text: Protected guest hypercall dispatcher examines the requested vendor function and either completes it locally with result registers updated or reports it as unhandled so the host can serve it. Local completions cover capability discovery plus memory information plus share plus unshare operations with invalid parameter as default result.

Capability discovery advertises a fixed small set covering discovery itself and memory information and share and unshare. Memory information demands that trailing arguments are clear and otherwise reports page granularity. Share and unshare demand that later arguments are clear and otherwise retain invalid parameter outcome.

Boot argument record used for power operations contains a synchronization cell together with a resume address together with a first argument value. Initialization sets the synchronization cell to unlocked state while leaving address and argument for later publication.

Each processor owns separate boot records for power on and for suspend, both starting unlocked. Unlocked and locked are distinct small integer states with unlocked as zero. The power on path observes published values under one shot semantics then releases reservation before entry, while resume consumes its own record.
Invalid processor identifier sentinel corresponds to the maximum value of its unsigned type.

Power entry helpers provide distinct noreturn targets for initial power on and for resume, both funneling into a common routine that records entry, installs first argument and target address into host context, establishes defined disabled memory management control and processor state, records exit, then transfers to host.
Host power configuration object is globally visible and fixed after early initialization.

Early setup retains processor count and computed per processor storage extent plus opaque bases for address translation structures and host second stage structures and self test area and proxy pages plus table operation vector plus allocation pool.
Hypervisor page allocation for tables uses zeroed single pages from the private pool, with reference acquisition and release delegated to pool helpers.

Ownership reconciliation accepts only valid leaf entries that refer to real memory and rejects other cases. Derived ownership is mirrored into hypervisor and host tracking, with hypervisor executable text mapped read only for host inspection and owned pages assigned to hypervisor, while shared states are cross recorded between sides.

Protection decoding for hypervisor entries starts from preserved software attribute bits. Execute permissions are inferred from execute never controls with a variant that distinguishes privileged and unprivileged forms on capable systems. Read allowance follows access permission encoding, with invalid entries yielding only software bits.

Final initialization brings up the full allocator from reserved table pages, prepares host second stage structures, installs table operation callbacks, repairs reference counts, establishes fixed mappings, reconciles and verifies ownership, initializes messaging proxy and virtual machine table, exercises self test, then publishes status through host context and enters host without returning.

Reference repair traverses the whole table address span and acquires valid pages to offset early allocation. Ownership repair traverses each recorded memory region through its linear mapping and additionally traverses each processor stack in its private range.

Nonvolatile backtrace state includes per processor overflow area with strong alignment plus a descriptor holding normal stack base plus overflow base plus saved frame plus saved program location, alongside a separate bounded per processor buffer used in protected mode.
Backtrace preparation chooses protected path or nonprotected path based on protected mode enablement.

Nonprotected recording snapshots stack limits and caller position for later host inspection. Protected recording unwinds across overflow followed by normal hypervisor stack, appending each location with a zero terminator while preserving space for terminator and stopping at capacity. An alternate build provides an empty recording operation.
Overflow limits derive from the current processor overflow base extended by its fixed extent. Hypervisor stack limits derive from the current processor recorded stack top reduced by its fixed extent.
Stack walker repeatedly offers the current location to a consumer and advances to the caller frame, halting when the consumer declines or when advancement reports failure.

Hypervisor keeps per processor host data plus saved hyp context plus active vector, together with global mask groups governing trap delegation for system and debug and second generation and interrupt controller accesses.
Protected system register trap handling first gives workaround logic a chance to consume the exit before protected logic, succeeding when either side handles it.

Protected register emulation decodes trapped access and target register, searches a restricted table, raises an undefined exception when absent, punts to host when marked host handled, otherwise invokes the registered handler with conditional instruction advancement and updates the target register on reads.

Synchronous exception synthesis must refresh guest program position and status from hypervisor exception state and synchronize virtualized control registers before pending the exception and adjusting position, then install fault syndrome and return state across levels. Undefined injection uses the unknown reason with length indication.

Trap dispatch uses separate tables for host hypervisor and protected guests indexed by exception class with unlisted classes unhandled. Both share handlers for SIMD extensions and low aborts and watchpoints and memory operations, while host handles coprocessor and system traps locally and protected guests route hypercalls and system traps to protected handlers and treat scalable vector traps as restricted.

Fatal hypervisor trap path is noreturn, snapshots processor status and return address and fault address state, and when a guest was running disables timers and traps and restores host translation and register state. It then captures backtrace context and enters common panic handling. A bad stack variant aliases this path, while unexpected level handling forwards to a common unexpected handler.

Feature ceiling descriptor records signedness plus field position plus field width plus allowed maximum plus an optional predicate that decides per virtual machine support. A zero width entry terminates a table.

Hypervisor retains sanitized values for architected identification registers across processor and memory and instruction families. Pointer authentication support requires build enablement plus hardware capability plus guest feature selection, while scalable vector support requires system availability plus guest feature selection.

Protected identifier tables impose per field ceilings for exception levels and floating and graphics and security and memory addressing and tagging and debug related fields, with scalable vector and pointer authentication ceilings gated by their respective predicates.
Certain debug and memory model fields use nonzero encodings to denote absence of the feature, covering double lock plus physical mutual exclusion plus second stage host extension signaling.

Identification register read returns zero with a one time warning when initialization has not completed, returns zero outside the architected identification range, and otherwise returns the stored per virtual machine value selected by encoding.

Read as zero write ignored emulation clears the value on reads and accepts writes without effect. Legacy thirty two bit identification access rejects writes by raising an undefined exception while reads behave as zero.
